Subject: Mutual action plan: throughput validation & unit-cost snapshot

Anika —

Great meeting yesterday. Per our discovery, Clearline's top priorities for the pilot are:
- Guaranteed TTFT (time-to-first-token) < 120ms for common flows
- Sustained throughput for peak batch processing (4k QPS target across the payment pipeline)
- Clear unit economics for 1M / 10M token volumes for decisioning workflows

I sketched a short MAP and a lightweight throughput evaluation plan attached. High level:
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize test corpus and access (we need an anonymized subset of production traffic + 5 synthetic stress prompts).
2) Week 1: run warmup + concurrency sweep (1, 4, 8, 16, 32 workers). Collect sustained QPS and tokens/sec.
3) Week 2: TTFT measurements and single-request latency SLA checks (p95, p99).
4) Week 3: unit economics run—measure tokens, GPU utilization, and project cost per 1M tokens under recommended batching / cache config.

Ask: can you confirm the anonymized sample will be ready Tuesday (5/18)? If so, Marcus will run our harness and share raw numbers + a short unit-cost sheet.

Attachments: map_v1.xlsx (MAP milestones), test_corpus_spec.md

Thanks —
Ethan

Anika —

Thanks — we've updated the MAP to include explicit fallback rules:
- Primary: Redwood-catalyst-v1 (intended for low latency).
- Fallback 1: Redwood-catalyst-v1-quant (4-bit) — lower cost, ~1.4x TTFT vs primary.
- Fallback 2: Redwood-costsave-small — used for sustained backfill processing with relaxed p99 SLA.

Ops actions (in MAP):
- On sustained QPS > 85% of threshold for 3 mins, route 20% of traffic to Fallback 1.
- On sustained QPS > 95% for 1 min, open circuit and route to Fallback 2 with throttling.

We will also include a short runbook for your SREs in the MAP. Marcus, plan the harness to capture failover metrics too.

Grace
Program Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: throughput validation & unit-cost snapshot

Hi all —

Attached are the raw results from the Redwood harness and a 1-page unit econ summary (attachments: throughput_results_20270520.csv, unit_econ_breakdown_20270520.pdf). Highlights below (test harness: 8x A100s, network 25 Gbps, 90s steady-state window per concurrency point):

Summary (primary model: redwood-catalyst-v1):
- Warmup: 60s warmup to fill KV cache.
- Concurrency sweep (workers):
  * 1 worker:  tokens/sec = 4,200; sustained QPS (requests/sec) = 95; median TTFT = 38ms; p99 TTFT = 112ms.
  * 4 workers: tokens/sec = 15,800; sustained QPS = 360; median TTFT = 42ms; p99 TTFT = 128ms.
  * 8 workers: tokens/sec = 29,600; sustained QPS = 680; median TTFT = 54ms; p99 TTFT = 153ms.
  * 16 workers: tokens/sec = 55,400; sustained QPS = 1,260; median TTFT = 71ms; p99 TTFT = 198ms.
  * 32 workers: tokens/sec = 96,000; sustained QPS = 2,100; median TTFT = 110ms; p99 TTFT = 245ms.

Sustained 4k QPS projection (based on linear scaling and our autoscale model):
- To reach ~4,000 sustained QPS for your peak batch window, estimate pool of 61 workers (8xA100 baseline) with recommended batching (avg tokens/request = 48). Expected p99 TTFT ~ 260-300ms under that scale; we recommend enabling the fallback routing described in the MAP for traffic spikes.

Unit economics (raw):
- Measured GPU time per 1M tokens: ~48 GPU-minutes (across the pool at 8xA100 baseline).
- Effective infrastructure cost per 1M tokens (cloud list rates): $12.60 (GPU + infra + network).
- With our recommended batching/caching config, projected cost per 1M tokens at your peak scale: $8.90 (volume discount model applied).
- Per-request cost (median request ~48 tokens): ~$0.00043 at projected scale.

Notes and caveats:
- TTFT numbers include network egress and tokenization overhead in our harness.
- Projections assume similar prompt distribution and an average 48 tokens per request; we can re-run if your real sample shows different token-length distribution.
- Attachments contain the CSV of point measurements and the unit econ calculations (breakdown by GPU-minutes, reserved vs spot mix, and amortized infra).

Next steps we recommend:
1) Review the attached CSV and call out any outlier prompts for a re-run.
2) Sign off on the MAP fallback thresholds so we can include them in the canary.
3) If agreed, we will prepare a short addendum to the proposal documenting the estimated monthly bill at 10M tokens and propose a Dedicated capacity recommendation.

Marcus
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
